subject: mathematics
question_text: For any three vectors a, b, c prove that [b×c  c×a  a×b] = [a b c]².

mark_split.label: Write the box product as a dot

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.104 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 159. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). Printed appearances: none — this answer carries no year tag. A pure identity with no numbers. The whole proof rests on ONE expansion — the vector triple product — plus the fact that a box product with a repeated vector is zero. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Write the box product as a dot
steps.margin_note: First mark. A box product [p q r] means p·(q×r). Apply that with p = b×c, q = c×a, r = a×b.
lines: By definition, [p q r] = p·(q × r).

recall.must_convey: That the box product is rewritten as (b×c)·[(c×a) × (a×b)].
accept: a box product is the first vector dotted with the cross of the other two
write it as b cross c dotted with c cross a crossed with a cross b
convert the box bracket into a dot and a cross
box product ante dot into cross
rewrite the left side using the definition

steps.why: The box bracket is only notation. Opening it into a dot and a cross is what exposes something the triple-product formula can act on.
common_mistakes: Expanding all three cross products separately into components.
Treating [p q r] as a product of magnitudes.

steps.label: Expand with the triple product
steps.margin_note: Three marks. Use (X × Y) = ... with X = c×a treated as a single vector: (c×a) × (a×b) = [(c×a)·b]a − [(c×a)·a]b.
lines: Treating (c×a) as one vector and using
= [c a b] a − [c a a] b

recall.must_convey: That the triple product expansion gives [c a b]a − [c a a]b.
accept: expand the cross of the two cross products to get c a b times a minus c a a times b
use the vector triple product with c cross a as one vector
the expansion gives two box products as coefficients
triple product tho expand cheste rendu box products vasthai
apply the vector triple product formula

steps.why: Each dot of (c×a) with another vector is itself a box product — that is what turns the expansion into scalars multiplying a and b.
common_mistakes: Getting the two terms the wrong way round.
Forgetting that the coefficients are scalars, not vectors.

steps.label: Kill the repeated term
steps.margin_note: Fifth mark, and the step the proof turns on. [c a a] has a REPEATED vector, so it is zero — the second term vanishes completely.
lines: A box product with a repeated vector is zero.

recall.must_convey: That [c a a] = 0 because a vector is repeated, so only the first term survives.
accept: c a a is zero because a vector repeats so the second term disappears
a box product with a repeated vector is zero
only the first term survives
repeat aina box product zero, so rendo term poyindi
the second term vanishes

steps.why: A box product measures a volume, and a box with two identical edges is flat — no volume. That is why any repeated vector makes it zero.
common_mistakes: Writing [c a a] as [c a b] by mistake.

steps.label: Dot with b×c
steps.margin_note: Two marks. [c a b] is a scalar, so it comes straight out of the dot product, leaving (b×c)·a — which is another box product.

recall.must_convey: That the scalar [c a b] factors out, leaving (b×c)·a = [b c a], so the left side is [c a b][b c a].
accept: the scalar comes out of the dot product leaving b cross c dotted with a which is the box product b c a
it becomes c a b times b c a
take the scalar outside and the rest is another box product
scalar bayata teesthe migilindi inko box product
the left side is a product of two box products

steps.why: A scalar multiplying a vector inside a dot product can always be pulled outside. What is left, (b×c)·a, is a box product by the same definition used in step 1.
common_mistakes: Leaving the scalar inside the dot.
Writing (b×c)·a as [a b c] without noting the order.

steps.label: Use the cyclic property
steps.margin_note: Last mark. A box product is unchanged by a cyclic shift, so [c a b] and [b c a] are BOTH equal to [a b c] — the product is [a b c]².
lines: A box product is unchanged by a cyclic shift:
[c a b] = [a b c]  and  [b c a] = [a b c]

recall.must_convey: That the cyclic property makes [c a b] = [b c a] = [a b c], so the left side is [a b c]².
accept: both box products equal a b c by the cyclic property so the answer is a b c squared
a cyclic shift does not change a box product
the product of the two equals a b c all squared
cyclic shift tho rendu a b c ye, so square vasthundi
the result is a b c squared

steps.why: A CYCLIC shift leaves a box product alone; swapping just two of the three flips its sign. Both shifts here are cyclic, so no sign appears in the answer.
common_mistakes: Treating any reordering as harmless and losing a sign.
Stopping at [c a b][b c a] without closing to [a b c]².
